We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{3},\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -\sqrt{3} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{3} & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{3} & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-2\sqrt{3},\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))=(1,\sqrt{3},0),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,-2\sqrt{3},\,0⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-\sqrt{3},\,z⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-1)-2\sqrt{3}\cdot (y-\sqrt{3})+0\cdot z & =0 \\ -2x-2\sqrt{3\,}y+8 & =0 \\ -x-\sqrt{3}\,y+4 & =0 \\ x+\sqrt{3}\,y & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(2cos⁡usin⁡v),∂∂u(2sin⁡usin⁡v),∂∂u(2cos⁡v)⟩=⟨−2sin⁡usin⁡v,2cos⁡usin⁡v,0⟩rv′(u,v)=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(2cos⁡usin⁡v),∂∂v(2sin⁡usin⁡v),∂∂v(2cos⁡v)⟩=⟨2cos⁡ucos⁡v,2sin⁡ucos⁡v,−2sin⁡v⟩

Next, we evaluate these vectors when u=π3 and v=π2:

ru′(π3,π2)=⟨−2sin⁡(π3)sin⁡(π2),2cos⁡(π3)sin⁡(π2),0⟩=⟨−3,1,0⟩rv′(π3,π2)=⟨2cos⁡(π3)cos⁡(π2),2sin⁡(π3)cos⁡(π2),−2sin⁡(π2)⟩=⟨0,0,−2⟩

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

n=ru′(π3,π2)×rv′(π3,π2)=|ijk−31000−2|=⟨|100−2|,−|−300−2|,|−3100|⟩=⟨−2,−23,0⟩.

Since the parameters u=π3 and v=π2 correspond to the point

(2cos⁡(π3)sin⁡(π2),2sin⁡(π3)sin⁡(π2),2cos⁡(π2))=(1,3,0),

the equation of the tangent plane is

n⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0⟨−2,−23,0⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−3,z⟩=0(−2)⋅(x−1)−23⋅(y−3)+0⋅z=0−2x−23y+8=0−x−3y+4=0x+3y=4.
